The task is to compute the bending stress at three fiber locations in a rectangular beam cross-section using the standard flexure formula under small-deformation, linear-elastic assumptions.
The cross-section is rectangular with width b = 50 mm and height h = 120 mm.
The internal bending moment at the section is given directly as M = 4,000,000 N·mm, sagging (no need to derive M from transverse loads or applied couples).
The vertical coordinate y is measured from the neutral axis (centroid of the rectangle), with positive direction upward.
The governing relation is the flexure formula: sigma = minus M times y divided by I, where I is the second moment of area of the rectangular section about the horizontal centroidal axis.
Compute I as I = b times h cubed divided by 12.
Evaluate sigma at three specified fiber locations: y = 0 mm (neutral axis), y = plus h/2 (top fiber), and y = minus h/2 (bottom fiber).
Report results in MPa (consistent with N and mm input units, since N·mm·mm divided by mm⁴ yields N/mm² = MPa).
State explicitly that the material is linear-elastic, deformations are small, plane sections remain plane, and the beam obeys Euler-Bernoulli bending theory.
No transverse shear, no axial force, no torsion, and no stress concentration effects are to be considered.
